text:
alex: Running nsys on the nightly runtime build and most CUDA kernels show up as <unknown> / no source lines. nvprof/nvtx traces also missing line info for device kernels. Anyone seen this recently?

maria: Hmm, did you build with debug/line flags? For device code you need -lineinfo (and -G if you want full device debug, but that kills perf).

alex: Yep, build had -g -O2 for host, and I added -lineinfo for nvcc. Still names are generic: kernel_0x7f... and perfetto timeline has no file:line.

praveen: Could be CUPTI / toolkit mismatch inside the container. If libcupti doesn't match the driver/toolkit used to compile you get poor symbol resolution. What base image are you using?

alex: docker image is nvidia/cuda:12.2-runtime-ubuntu22.04. Host driver is 535.x. I mounted the build artifacts into the container.

maria: Did you strip the binary after build or run a post-build packaging step that removes debug sections? Also check nvcc's --keep option: sometimes device code gets moved into cubin/sass and source mappings get lost if intermediate files are removed.

alex: Not stripping. Build output shows cubin sections present. I tried running:

```
nsys profile --trace=cuda,nvtx -o /tmp/nsys_run ./bin/redwood-runtime --profile-workload
```

and then opened the .nsys-rep in the UI: kernel names are addresses, hover shows no file/line. CLI nsys export shows same.

praveen: Try setting CUPTI_VERBOSE=1 to see CUPTI warnings. Also check CUPTI lib path: LD_LIBRARY_PATH inside container should point to the /usr/local/cuda/extras/CUPTI/lib64 that matches the toolkit used to build. If you're mounting build artifacts from a different host toolkit, symbol lookup can fail.

alex: Ran with CUPTI_ENV: CUPTI_LIB64_PATH=/usr/local/cuda/extras/CUPTI/lib64 and CUPTI_VERBOSE=1. Output shows:

```
CUPTI Warning: API mismatch - CUPTI header version 12.2 != libcupti version 12.1
Symbol resolution may be limited.
```

maria: There you go. Header/header vs runtime lib mismatch. If you compiled against 12.2 headers but runtime CUPTI is 12.1 you'll lose line info. Options: rebuild with the container's toolkit, upgrade libcupti inside container, or vendor the exact libcupti.so into your runtime image.

alex: Rebuilt the container with cuda:12.2-base and installed matching libcupti from toolkit. Rerun shows more kernel names but still no file:line for several kernels (mostly fused kernels from the transformer fused-kernel path).

praveen: Fused kernels sometimes get inlined/split by compiler; -lineinfo may not be propagated into final cubin if PTX->SASS steps drop debug. Try building with NVCC flag -Xptxas -lineinfo and also keep ptx: --keep or nvcc -keep to retain intermediate .ptx/.sass. That can help nsys map back. Also ensure you didn't use --strip-all on the cubin.

alex: Good tip. I rebuilt with: nvcc ... -g -lineinfo -Xptxas=-v -Xptxas=-lineinfo -keep, and copied the intermediate .ptx into the container. Now nsys shows source file names for ~80% of kernels, but a handful still show address-only.

maria: For those remaining, inspect the ELF(/cubin) symbol table. Use cuobjdump --dump-sass and cuobjdump --dump-lineinfo on the cubin to see if line mappings exist. If cuobjdump doesn't show lineinfo, the line info isn't present and nsys can't invent it.

alex: Ran cuobjdump --dump-lineinfo on the offending cubin: it prints nothing for those kernels. cuobjdump --dump-sass shows SASS for them, so codegen happened but no line table.

praveen: Two possibilities: upstream PTX was generated without line directives, or ptxas step optimized out or merged those regions. Search the compiler/linker flags for --relocatable-device-code or LTO-like flags. Also check if you used device-side linking (separate compilation) — lineinfo can be lost if device linking performed without preserving debug anchors.

alex: We're using device linking (nvlink) for separate compilation across translation units. I did notice our build uses -rdc=true. Could that be it?

maria: -rdc=true enables relocatable device code and requires proper device linking; make sure nvcc/nglink/nvlink versions align. Also try building a minimal repro with -rdc=false or compile the problematic kernel in the same TU to see if the lineinfo appears. If it does, it's a device-linker issue.

alex: Minimal repro with -rdc=false shows lineinfo for the kernel. So it's the device link phase. Any tips to preserve it across nvlink?

praveen: Ensure you pass -lineinfo at both compile and link nvlink stages. Some build systems only propagate it to compilation but not to nvlink. Also check CUDA_NVCC_FLAGS and NVLINK flags. For example: nvcc -dlink -lineinfo ... and nvlink --lineinfo ... (depending on versions).

alex: I added -lineinfo to the dlink step and to nvlink invocation. Now cuobjdump --dump-lineinfo shows mappings and nsys/pfetto show file:line for everything.

alex: Final note: also verify package runtime isn't replacing libcupti with older version (k8s node driver plugin mount). We saw a cluster node with older libcupti symlinking into the container and it silently broke resolution.

maria: Great checklist: 1) compile with -g/-lineinfo (-Xptxas flags as needed) 2) keep intermediate PTX if debugging (-keep) 3) ensure libcupti inside runtime matches headers/toolkit + set CUPTI_LIB64_PATH 4) add -lineinfo at dlink/nvlink 5) check docker host mounts for conflicting libcupti.

alex: Thanks all — saving this thread as a recipe for next perf triage. infra-bot: please tag the perf-playbook issue with "cupti-debug" and add link to this thread.

infra-bot: Created issue PERF-482: "Investigate CUPTI/toolkit mismatches and device-link lineinfo" and linked this thread. :white_check_mark:
